Will your love letter woo the Princess and win her heart? Utilize the characters in the castle to secretly carry your message to the Princess, earning her affection. Love Letter is a game of risk, deduction, and luck. Designed by Seiji Kanai, the game features simple rules that create dynamic and fun player interactions. Players attempt to deliver their love letter into the Princess’s hands while keeping other players’ letters away. Powerful cards lead to early gains, but make you a target. Rely on weaker cards for too long and your letter may be tossed in the fire! Number of players: 2 - 6 Game duration: 23 mn Complexity: 1 / 5 Play Love Letter and 1414 other games online. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Theme 2 Setup 3 Game play 3.1 Round End 3.1.1 Tiebreak 4 Game end Theme In the wake of the arrest of Queen Marianna for high treason, none was more heartbroken than her daughter, Princess Annette. Suitors throughout the City-State of Tempest sought to ease Annette's sorrow by courting her to bring some joy into her life. You are one of these suitors, trying to get your love letter to the princess. Unfortunately, she has locked herself in the palace, so you must rely on intermediaries to carry your message. During the game, you hold one secret card in your hand. This is who currently carries your message of love for the princess. Make sure that the person closest to the princess holds your love letter at the end of the day, so it reaches her first! Setup One of the 16 playing cards is removed at the beginning of each round and the others are shuffled. Every player is dealt one card. The remaining cards form a pile in the centre of the table. Game play Players take turns drawing one card (making two cards in hand) and discarding one card (returning to one card in hand). When a player discards a card, its effect is applied. Card effects - 2-4 players (Classic) Value № Name Simplified effect description Full effect description 8 1 Princess Annette Discard = out! If you discard the Princess — no matter how or why — she has tossed your letter into the fire. You are knocked out of the round. 7 1 Countess Wilhelmina Must discard with King or Prince in hand Unlike other cards which take effect when discarded, the text on the Countess applies while she is in your hand. In fact, she has no effect when you discard her. If you ever have the Countess and either the King or Prince in your hand, you must discard the Countess. You do not have to reveal the other card in your hand. Of course, you can also discard the Countess even if you do not have a royal family member in your hand. She likes to play mind games. 6 1 King Arnaud IV Swap hands When you discard King Arnaud IV, trade the card in your hand with the card held by another player of your choice. You cannot trade with a player who is out of the round, nor with someone protected by the Handmaid. If all other players still in the round are protected by the Handmaid, this card does nothing. 5 2 Prince Arnaud A player must discard When you discard Prince Arnaud, choose one player still in the round (including yourself). That player discards their hand (do not apply its effect, unless it's Princess Annette) and draws a new card. If the deck is empty, that player draws the card that was removed at the start of the round. If all other players are protected by the Handmaid, you must choose yourself. 4 2 Handmaid Susannah May not be targeted When you discard the Handmaid, you are immune to the effects of other players’ cards until the start of your next turn. 3 2 Baron Talus Compare -> lower = out When discarded, choose one other player still in the round. You and that player secretly compare your hands. The player with the lower rank is knocked out of the round. In case of a tie, nothing happens. [Rating: 1/10] Very very minimalistic. Well done for making a filler game that is accessible to everyone with just around 10 cards. However, I find the game very restricted on what you can do.

[Rating: 1/10] Same as Love Letter, the additional charactersa aren't a meaningful enough addition to change my opinion on the game.

[Rating: 2/10] It's barely a game, but at least it's fast.  [b]Pros:[/b] The deduction aspect that the Guard allows for at least lends the game some actual gameplay.   There's some fun bluffing to be done with the Courtesan.   [b]Cons:[/b] Well, the game has player elimination and take-that. People don't usually care because the game is so fast, but I still don't think it's good design.   It's also so feather-light that we might as well, you know, actually just talk to each other? [Rating: 2/10] Basically a game that plays itself especially when you have the princess. You only get two choices until you get a princess then it's just going through the motions because you'll just lose if you play the princess, but it's also obvious you have the princess. It's not fun at all.

[Rating: 2/10] As a newcomer to Love Letter, it just seemed like a case of he who knows the deck inside out wins and a silly meta that had already been long established by the people who owned it.  I disliked this for the same reasons I'd never choose Rock, Paper, Scissors to decide a game.

[Rating: 3/10] Overrated garbage. I don't know if I've ever been less interested in a game while playing it. I just couldn't care about a single second of this game.
